chunks: And that which was narrated is: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Wassha' from Aban from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who divorces his wife while she is pregnant, can he marry her sister before she gives birth? He said: He does not marry her until her period of waiting is complete. For it is understood that if he divorced her with a revocable divorce, as indicated by what we have previously mentioned in the narrations, and it included that if he divorced her with an irrevocable divorce, it is permissible for him to contract marriage with her sister even if she has not exited the waiting period. Those narrations are detailed, and this report is general, and the ruling based on the detailed is preferred over the general.

As for the Mut'ah (temporary marriage) wife, it has been narrated regarding her that if her fixed term expires, it is not permissible to contract marriage with her sister except after the completion of her waiting period.
And al-Husayn ibn Sa'id also narrated, saying: I read in the book of a man to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him)

May I be your ransom, a man marries a woman for temporary marriage to a specified term, and the term expires between them. Is he permitted to marry her sister before her waiting period expires? He wrote (in reply) (peace be upon him): It is not permissible for him to marry her until her waiting period expires.

key_terms.رَجْعَتَهَا: Her right of revocation (in revocable divorce)

ai.seo_question: Can a man marry two sisters if one is divorced while pregnant or in temporary marriage?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent contradiction between this general report and more specific narrations by applying the principle of *al-hukm bi-l-mufassal 'ala l-mujmal* (the specific ruling prevails over the general), clarifying that the prohibition applies strictly to permanent divorce where the husband retains revocability. The text further distinguishes the ruling for *Mut'ah* (temporary marriage), where the waiting period (*Iddah*) must fully elapse before marrying the sister, highlighting the nuanced jurisprudential distinctions between permanent and temporary marital contracts in Shia fiqh.
